newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 4.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 4.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST...
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
ATLANTA - Telephone company BellSouth Corp announces a new $20 million television ad campaign aimed at local phone service competition from AT&T Corp and other companies.

HERGISWIL, Switzerland - Swiss advertising spending fell 0.3 percent in May from May 1996 and was up 1.0 percent in the first five months of 1997, according to data compiled by the Media Focus agency.
LONDON - M&C Saatchi Australia has won the advertising account for the Australian newspaper following a pitch against Y&R Mattingly, Foote Cone & Belding and Batey Kazoo.

HELSINKI - Estimated advertising spending in Finland rose 7.5 percent year-on-year to 2.09 billion markka ($401.2 million) in January-May, research firm Gallup-Mainostieto says. Newspaper advertising rose 4.0 percent to 1.20billion markka.
WASHINGTON - A U.S. labour federation will start running radio advertisements this weekend claiming the North American Free Trade Agreement is taking jobs away from American workers.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - French pay television group Canal Plus says it expects to make a profit of some three billion francs ($508.5 million) from selling its 37.5 percent stake in German pay television group Premiere to Kirch.

LONDON - British newspaper company Mirror Group Plc says it has arranged a five-year 600 million pound ($1 billion) credit facility to refinance its debt and pay for its planned acquisition of Midland Independent Newspapers Plc.
MUNICH - Shares in German television channel Pro Sieben, due to be floated on the stock market on Monday, are likely to be than 10 times oversubscribed, a spokesman for the company says.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong wants to remain a major regional broadcasting hub and to maintain its media strength, the fledgling government says. "Hong Kong faces stiff competition from other locations in the region," says a government official.
PARIS, - France says it welcomes an appeal by U.S. President Bill Clinton for a laissez-faire policy on Internet commerce but says young people and consumers should be protected.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

CALCUTTA - India, the world's second most populous nation, is set for a sharp rise in condom use over the next decade from around one per person annually, a spokesman for British condom firm London International Group Plc, maker of the Durex brand, says.
TOKYO - Sales of imported vehicles in Japan fell 20.5 percent in June from a year earlier to 32,176 units, the Japan Automobile Importers' Association says.
BONN - Germany's new telecommunications regulatory chief, says his main focus will be to ensure a fair playing field for newcomers to the market.
TOKYO - Compaq Computer Corp, the world's top seller of personal computers, says it plans an ambitious push to increase its market share in Japan where it has been struggling to compete.

NEW DELHI - India's information technology industry, including hardware and software, grew 38 per cent to a revenue of 134.34 billion rupees ($3.75 billion) in 1996/97 (April-March), India's Dataquest magazine says.
BRUSSELS - Price-fixing companies beware! the European Commission's top cartel buster European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert warns that his department has never been so busy.
ADELAIDE - The Australian wine immediate challenge is to establish a foothold in Asia without compromising its drive into Europe and North America, the Australian Wine Export Council says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

SYDNEY - Carbonated "new-age" drinks are losing their fizz after just five years on the market, but more health-oriented beverages are gaining in stamina says the Australian Soft Drink Association. Australian Consumers guzzle about $70 million worth of sports drinks a year, it says.
BERLIN - The Love Parade, a giant techno party expected to attract a million young people from around the world to Berlin on July 12, may be moved to other cities in future, its organisers say.
LONDON - London is reviving its Victorian public loos for tourists, say tourist officials.
